name: validate_that
title: Validate that certain conditions are true.

origin.description: validate_that returns a message instead of stopping.

arguments.text: Unnamed expressions that describe the conditions.

arguments.name: env
arguments.text: The environment in which to evaluate the assertions.

arguments.name: msg
arguments.text: A custom message if one of the conditions is false.

origin.details: Returns TRUE when every assertion is TRUE. Otherwise it returns the failure message as a string.

translation.description: validate_that returns a message instead of stopping.

arguments.name: env
arguments.text: A dict of names. When omitted, names come from the caller's locals.

arguments.name: msg
arguments.text: A custom message if one of the conditions is false.

translation.details: Returns True when every assertion is true. Otherwise it returns the failure message as a string. Expressions are strings.
translation.example:
from assertthat import validate_that

x = 1
print(validate_that("is.numeric(x)"))
print(validate_that("is.character(x)"))
print(validate_that("length(x) == 3"))
print(validate_that('is.dir("asdf")'))
